purpose: Teach: うり/錦/メロディー/ギリシア/壁紙/禅/春樹/マニアック

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 夏のうり、若い頃、田舎で、よく食べたな、私たち、覚えてる?
lines.en: Summer melon — I remember we used to eat it so often when we were young, out in the country.
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Gentle questioning at the end, not demanding confirmation but inviting her into the recollection. Slow, unhurried pace. The warmth of a shared past.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。新婚旅行、京都の錦市場、二人で、歩いたわね、楽しかった。
lines.en: Yes. Our honeymoon in Kyoto, at Nishiki Market — we walked through there together. It was such a good time.
lines.style: Animated remembering. Brightness surfaces in her voice as the image becomes clear. Her pace quickens slightly with affection. Small smile audible at the edges.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、君がピアノで弾いたメロディー、今でも、覚えているよ。
lines.en: When you were young, I still remember the melody you played on piano. The notes are still with me.
lines.style: Tenderness weighted with time. Pause before 'still remember' — a small breath of gratitude that the memory persists. Quiet, almost careful. Like holding something precious.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: ギリシア神話の本、子供たちに、読み聞かせたわね、夜。
lines.en: We read Greek myths to the children at night — do you remember? I'd read those stories aloud to them.
lines.style: Voice carries the echo of her own voice from decades ago. Not quite present-tense, but not quite past either — suspended in the act of remembering. Softer than speech, almost murmuring.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 新婚の家、壁紙、二人で、選んだよな、覚えてる、ばあさん?
lines.en: When we first got married, we chose the wallpaper for that house together. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Gentle insistence. Not challenging her memory but reaching for her — wanting her to hold this moment with him. Warmth underneath, a small lift of affection on 'together'.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 禅寺、毎年、お盆に、お参り、行ってきたわね、二人で。
lines.en: Every Obon, we'd visit that Zen temple together, year after year. Just the two of us.
lines.style: Rhythm of ritual in her voice. Each phrase lands with the weight of repetition — the comfort of annual return. Slow, measured. A meditation more than a statement.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 息子の春樹、最近、孫を、連れて、よく訪ねてくれるな。
lines.en: Our son Haruki has been visiting so much lately — bringing the grandchildren with him. It's good.
lines.style: Quiet pride and contentment. Not boasting, observing. A soft exhale of gratitude that the family circle continues. Warmth without sentiment.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: あなた、若い頃、マニアックな趣味、いっぱい、持っていたわよね。
lines.en: You had all sorts of strange hobbies when you were young, didn't you? I remember you were quite the character.
lines.style: Affectionate teasing just beneath the surface. A half-smile in her voice. Warm, slightly wry — the kind of observation only someone who loved him through those years could make. Intimate and playful.
